tech_debt.summary: No automated unit or integration tests exist. src/test/java contains only CatastrophicEventsPluginTest.main(), a manual dev-launcher that boots a full RuneLite client for eyeballing - not a real test.

Gson and OkHttp versions are not pinned in build.gradle - both are pulled in transitively via net.runelite:client, which itself resolves to 'latest.release'. Builds are not reproducible; a RuneLite client update can silently change JSON parsing or HTTP behavior underneath the plugin with no version diff to point at.

known_issues.summary: No endpoint returns a Discord guild ID, so guildId must be manually entered by each user in config rather than fetched from the API - documented as a known gap in README.md.

The events API response has no `host` field yet (backend Event model has hostDiscordId but GET /events doesn't return it) - both EventHeroCard and EventCompactRow omit the Host row entirely rather than showing a placeholder, per README's documented decision.

No 'expected world' field exists on events yet, so EventHeroCard's World row is hardcoded to the literal string 'Not set by host yet' and no auto-check-in logic (comparing against client.getWorld()) can be built.

poc-runelite-plugin.md (the original scope/design doc) still documents the old /api/plugin/* endpoint paths hosted by catabot-web; the actual bot API used today has no /api/plugin prefix (GET {apiBase}/events, POST {apiBase}/signup). The design doc is stale and should not be trusted for endpoint paths - README.md has the corrected paths.

warnings.summary: This plugin has a hard runtime dependency on a sibling repo's HTTP API contract (catabot's PLUGIN_API_PORT server, ../catabot on disk) that is not versioned, mocked, or tested from within this repo. Gson's fromJson does not fail loudly on missing/renamed fields, so a breaking change to catabot's /events or /signup response shape would silently degrade (nulls) rather than error clearly here.

EventDto.minutesUntilStart() throws on an unparsable start_at. The plugin's own reminder loop (checkReminderMilestones) catches this per-event and silently skips it, while the UI layer duplicates the same null-safety logic independently via a separate safeMinutesUntilStart() wrapper in EventHeroCard - the guard is implemented twice rather than centralized on the DTO.

The plugin token is stored in RuneLite's ConfigManager with only UI-level masking (secret=true) - this is a deliberate, documented design decision (poc-runelite-plugin.md), not an oversight. Do not 'fix' this without confirming the intended trust model with the project owner first.
apiBase defaults to plain HTTP (http://localhost:8080) and nothing warns or blocks a user from pointing it at a non-local, non-TLS host - the Bearer token would then travel in cleartext.

AlertsApiClient duplicates EventsApiClient's 401/unsuccessful/network error-classification logic inline instead of sharing a helper (logged as an anticipated deviation, WL-5 on discord-loot-death-coffer-alerts) - a future change to that classification logic has to be made in two places or it'll silently drift.

PetDropListener and OneTimeRewardListener (fire cape / infernal cape / Dizana's quiver) match on best-effort recalled chat-message wording that has not been confirmed against a live client actually producing those messages (can't fake a real pet drop or Inferno completion in dev). If the wording is off, the affected alert would silently just never fire - no error, no crash. Confirm against real chat log text (or a clan member's report) the first time each of these actually fires, and tighten the Pattern if it turns out wrong.
warnings.resolution_note: Resolves the spoofing half of this concern: both listeners now filter to ChatMessageType.GAMEMESSAGE before matching text, so a player typing matching text in public/clan/private chat can no longer trigger a false alert (confirmed exploitable via a real Discord incident before this fix; verified the GAMEMESSAGE filter against the 'Discord Notifications' Hub plugin's equivalent, real, previously-trusted check). PetDropListener's wording is now also confirmed correct for the primary pet message via a live screenshot. OneTimeRewardListener's exact fire cape/infernal cape/Dizana's quiver wording remains unconfirmed against a live client - if it's off, the alert will still just silently never fire, same residual risk as before, now tracked as WRN-007.

warnings.summary: OneTimeRewardListener's fire cape / infernal cape / Dizana's quiver chat-text wording (FIRE_CAPE_TOPIC/INFERNAL_CAPE_TOPIC/DIZANAS_QUIVER_TOPIC/COMPLETION_VERB patterns) is still best-effort/unconfirmed against a live client producing those exact messages - narrowed down from WRN-006, which the spoofing half of this concern (ChatMessageType filtering) now resolves. If the wording is off, the affected alert would silently just never fire - no error, no crash. Confirm against real chat log text the first time each of these actually fires, and tighten the Pattern if it turns out wrong.

net.runelite.api.ItemID (used by LootAlertListener's TRACKED_ACCOMPLISHMENT_ITEM_IDS allowlist, all 7 entries) is a deprecated class as of the currently-resolved RuneLite client version, superseded by net.runelite.api.gameval.ItemID. Confirmed via javac -Xlint:deprecation ("ItemID in net.runelite.api has been deprecated") - a class-level deprecation affecting every constant referenced from it, not specific to any one item. Pre-existing (was already true when these constants lived in the now-deleted AccomplishmentLootListener.java), just newly surfaced/documented here. Migrating to the gameval class needs each constant name re-verified for an exact match (not guaranteed 1:1) - not done as part of this fix to keep scope bounded to the loot-listener consolidation bug.

dependencies_at_risk.reason: Pinned to 'latest.release' rather than a fixed version - every build can silently pick up a newer RuneLite client API with no lockfile, making breakage hard to reproduce or bisect.
dependencies_at_risk.mitigation: Pin to a specific released version and bump deliberately; consider a CI job that builds against the pin to catch upstream breakage early.

dependencies_at_risk.reason: Also pinned to 'latest.release'; test-scope only, so lower blast radius, but same reproducibility risk as net.runelite:client.
JUnit 4.12 (2017) is superseded by 4.13.x / JUnit 5. Currently unused for real tests (see TD-001), so the risk is latent rather than active.
dependencies_at_risk.mitigation: Upgrade when real unit tests are introduced; consider adopting JUnit 5 at that point instead of bumping in place.
